post.title: How Lotus Hospital Improved Daily Operations with Healthray
post.excerpt: Lotus Hospital is a 200-bed multispeciality hospital in Valsad, Gujarat, with four operation theatres and critical care facilities. Its admissions, surgical, nursing and pharmacy workflows are now more streamlined, helping teams manage daily operations more efficiently.

seo.title: Lotus Hospital Case Study: 30% Faster Bed Allocation | Healthray
seo.description: See how Lotus Hospital in Valsad made bed allocation 30% faster, cut OT scheduling conflicts by 25% and reduced medicine wastage by 20% with Healthray.

fields.hero_lede: Lotus Hospital is a 200-bed multispeciality hospital in Valsad, Gujarat, with four operation theatres and critical care facilities. Its admissions, surgical, nursing and pharmacy workflows are now more streamlined, helping teams manage daily operations more efficiently.
overview_content: Lotus Hospital provides medical and surgical care, supported by dialysis, radiology, laboratory and pharmacy facilities. Its radiology department offers digital X-ray, sonography, colour Doppler and CT services.

As the hospital managed these activities across different teams, staff needed timely information to allocate beds, schedule procedures, hand over patient updates, and monitor medicine stock. Gaps in these workflows could slow down routine operations and make important updates harder to track.
fields.problem_heading: Four Workflow Gaps Affecting Daily Operations

problems.title: Bed status gaps
problems.text: Staff had to check whether beds were occupied, available or ready during admissions and transfers. Delayed bed-status updates could slow allocation.

problems.title: OT scheduling conflicts
problems.text: Teams had to manage theatre availability and procedure timings across four operating theatres. Schedule changes could lead to conflicts between procedures.

problems.title: Missed nursing updates
problems.text: Important patient updates could be missed during shift handovers when information was passed between nursing teams, leaving incoming staff without key updates.

problems.title: Late expiry tracking
problems.text: Pharmacy teams had to monitor medicine expiry dates across stock. Late identification of near-expiry medicines left less time to act.

fields.decision_intro: In order to manage the admissions process, OT schedules, nursing workflows and pharmaceuticals at Lotus Hospital, there was a need for a more structured approach. The hospital selected the Healthray software, where all these aspects can be managed digitally in one system.
fields.quote_text: Managing different workflows across departments was challenging, especially when teams needed to coordinate information. Healthray has brought these workflows together on one platform, making it easier for our teams to access information, coordinate their work and manage daily operations. We have found it much easier to keep things organised across departments.
fields.solution_heading: How Healthray helped Lotus improve hospital workflows

solutions.title: Bed & Ward Management
solutions.text: Bed status was managed through a central workflow, helping staff check occupied, available and ready beds during admissions and transfers and allocate beds more efficiently.

solutions.title: OT Management
solutions.text: OT schedules and theatre availability were managed digitally, helping teams coordinate procedures across the operating theatres and reduce scheduling conflicts.

solutions.title: IPD EMR & Nursing
solutions.text: Patient updates were recorded in IPD workflows, giving nursing teams a structured way to review information during shift handovers and reducing missed updates.

solutions.title: Pharmacy Management
solutions.text: Medicine stock and expiry information was managed digitally, helping pharmacy teams identify near-expiry medicines earlier and take action before they became unusable.

fields.setup_intro: Lotus Hospital worked with Healthray to transition its existing workflows to the new system.

steps.title: Workflows configured
steps.text: The hospital's existing processes were configured in the system.

steps.title: Existing information transferred
steps.text: Relevant hospital data was migrated into the configured workflows.

steps.title: Teams trained for daily use
steps.text: Staff were trained on the workflows relevant to their roles.

fields.results_intro: After implementing Healthray, Lotus Hospital improved its day-to-day operations.

results.title: faster bed allocation
results.text: Staff spent less time checking bed availability, allowing beds to be assigned faster during admissions and transfers.

results.title: fewer OT scheduling conflicts
results.text: Fewer clashes between procedures made it easier for teams to keep OT schedules organised.

results.title: fewer missed nursing updates
results.text: Incoming nursing staff had better access to the information they needed during shift handovers, reducing missed patient updates.

results.title: less medicine wastage
results.text: Pharmacy teams had more time to act on medicines approaching expiry, helping reduce avoidable wastage.

ba_rows.before: Staff checked bed status during admissions and transfers
ba_rows.after: Bed availability was centrally managed for quicker allocation

ba_rows.before: Theatre availability and procedure timings were managed separately
ba_rows.after: Theatre schedules and procedure timings were coordinated in one place

ba_rows.before: Patient updates could be missed during shift changes
ba_rows.after: Nursing teams could record and review patient updates during handovers

ba_rows.before: Near-expiry medicines could be identified late
ba_rows.after: Pharmacy teams could track expiry information and act earlier
